When a customer abandons checkout, their seats are held as a temporary reservation that expires after 10 minutes without payment; a worker scans for lapsed holds every 30 seconds, returns the seats to inventory, and invalidates the event page cache (and if Paylane confirms payment late on an already-lapsed hold, an automatic refund is triggered).

Sources: tidewater/memory/glossary.md, tidewater/plans/2026-04-01-hold-release-worker.md, tidewater/plans/2026-01-25-checkout-flow.md

When a customer abandons checkout, the seats are held for only 10 minutes (a "hold"); if payment doesn't complete in that window, the `tide-worker` process (scanning every 30 seconds) releases the seats back into inventory and invalidates the event page cache — a late Paylane confirmation arriving after that lapse triggers an automatic refund instead of re-blocking the seats.

Sources: tidewater/memory/glossary.md, tidewater/plans/2026-04-01-hold-release-worker.md

This is well-covered in the vault: high-demand on-sales are handled by routing buyers to a virtual waiting room (queue page on Nimbus CDN, token-bucket admitting 500 buyers/minute with a 15-minute signed pass) while workers are pre-scaled via the scale-worker-pool procedure; this design followed ADR-012 after the 2026-04-25 drop caused timeouts and Paylane rate-limit errors, and it proved itself on 2026-05-30 with 12,000 buyers queued and zero timeouts.

Certificates renew automatically every ~60 days via a certbot systemd timer (DNS challenge) with a deploy hook that rebuilds the HAProxy bundle and reloads it without downtime, alerting if a cert has <14 days left; if that automation fails, the manual fallback is `certbot renew --cert-name tidewater.example --force-renewal` on `kelp-1`, then rebuild the HAProxy bundle and `systemctl reload haproxy`.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-05-18-automazione-tls.md, tidewater/skills/rinnovo-certificati-tls.md

TLS renewal is normally automatic: certbot runs on a systemd timer every 12 hours with a DNS challenge against the domain provider, and a deploy hook rebuilds HAProxy's cert bundle and reloads it with zero downtime (an alert fires if a cert is within 14 days of expiry). If that automation fails, the manual fallback is on `kelp-1`: `sudo certbot renew --cert-name tidewater.example --force-renewal`, then rebuild the HAProxy bundle (`/usr/local/bin/haproxy-cert-bundle tidewater.example`) and `systemctl reload haproxy`.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-05-18-automazione-tls.md, tidewater/skills/rinnovo-certificati-tls.md
